newsitem.title: MEXICO: INSTANT VIEW -Mexico Dec CPI seen cheering markets.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW -Mexico Dec CPI seen cheering markets.

text.p: A better-than-expected inflation performance in December is likely to further cheer Mexico's buoyant financial markets and suggests January inflation will also be lower than some had feared, economists said on Thursday.

"It means second half of December inflation was up one percent, which is a very good number. It's a little bit of a surprise," said Gray Newman of HSBC James Capel. He lowered his January estimate to 2.5 percent from above 2.6 percent as a result of the December number.

"The market should take it well," another economist said of the 3.2 percent hike in the consumer price index. In a Reuters survey this week, analysts had predicted an average increase of 3.47 percent.
Economists said the December figure may have been lower than expected because price hikes of tortillas and milk on Dec. 30 spilt over into the first half of January.
Though that may push up the CPI early this month, the downward trend in the second half of December should mean a lower number in the month of January as a whole, they said.
Inflation in the first half of December was 2.34 percent.
"It's still almost twice as high as November and was higher than almost everyone had expected (before the first half of December number was released)," Newman said.
"But it does demonstrate a very strong decline in the rate of growth of prices in the second half of December."
The annual CPI growth was 27.70 percent, higher than the government's 20.5 percent forecast but closely in line with analysts' estimates.
Alonso Cervera of Interacciones in New York predicted the government would have a harder time bringing down inflation next year because of what he described as "repressed inflation".
He said producers would try to recuperate margins lost during the drastic sales slump in the last two years, adding that some freeing up of prices was not necessarily a problem.
"Perhaps its healthier to grow with some inflation than to try and kill inflation in a single blow," he said.
Newman noted that the 1996 inflation performance was almost half 1995's figure of 51.97 percent, and was far better than many economists had expected at the start of last year.
In 1997, he said there was a narrower cluster of forecasts. The government is gunning for 15 percent inflation this year, and most analysts predictions are in the range of 17-19 percent.
